_note: The Go/No-Go rules' figures and boundaries, written down from the Aviation Weather Handbook, 14 CFR 91.103, 91.133 and 91.137-91.145, the AIM and the PHAK, never from the code. Shape and checks as engine/facade/tests/common/cases.rs says; asked by engine/facade/tests/rule_cases.rs.

cases.name: 6,000 ft flown over a 5,000 ft freezing level in the moisture: icing possible
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-28B (Aviation Weather Handbook) ch. 20: structural icing needs visible moisture at a temperature at or below 0 C, so an altitude at or above the freezing level, in the moisture, may ice; one below it does not. A PIREP of NEG icing reports none (AIM 7-1-20).

cases.name: A TFR of 16:00 to 18:00Z, the flight there An hour before: before
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.137-91.145: a TFR binds from its effective to its expiry time; the rule widens that by its own margin, 30 minutes either side, so a flight near its edges is told of it (the safer side); one with no times is in force.

cases.name: Adverse conditions: the crossed TFR and the Convective SIGMET stop, then the CWA; the AIRMET one more
cases.source: AIM 7-1-5(b)(1): a standard briefing gives first the adverse conditions, "significant meteorological and/or aeronautical information that might influence the pilot to alter or cancel the proposed flight": a TFR the route crosses (14 CFR 91.137-91.145) and a Convective SIGMET or SIGMET (AIM 7-1-6) before a CWA, an urgent PIREP (UUA, AIM 7-1-18) or an AIRMET. A routine PIREP, a TFR only near the route and a SIGMET over before the flight are not adverse conditions on it.

cases.name: Runway findings: each field named once, in the route's order, under each flag it has
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): "For any flight, runway lengths at airports of intended use, and ... takeoff and landing distance information"; the checks' flags are gonogo_runway_checks' (over the runway, past the POH's table, past its demonstrated crosswind, under SAFO 19001's 15 per cent to spare, the length or elevation not known).

cases.name: Runway findings: calm along the end is no tailwind, half a knot behind is
cases.source: AIM 4-3-6: the runway most nearly into the wind; a wind along the end below zero is behind the airplane (gonogo_runway_checks' headwind_kt, negative for a tailwind).

cases.name: Runway findings: a length not known leaves the field unchecked; an empty reason does not
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): with no runway length, whether the distances fit is not known, never "within".

cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): "For any flight, runway lengths at airports of intended use, and ... takeoff and landing distance information"; the checks' flags are gonogo_runway_checks' (over the runway, past the POH's table, past its demonstrated crosswind, under SAFO 19001's 15 per cent to spare, the length or elevation not known).

cases.name: Runway findings: an airplane with no landing table is not worked
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b)(1): the distances are the airplane flight manual's; without its landing table they cannot be worked out.
